title: Registry index shard — /registry/index/{shard}.json (and the bulk export)
description: One shard of the published registry index, sharded by the first character of the repository name plus a `0` shard for everything non-alphabetic (FS02-062). THE SAME DOCUMENT SHAPE serves the bulk export `/registry/export.json` (apex alias `/registry.json`, FS10-060): that document sets `shard: "export"` and carries every entry. Entries are the minimum a browse page or a scanner needs; the full per-repository facts live in the repo record, whose URL each entry carries. Only `verified`, `suspended`, `quit` and `delisted` repositories appear — `detected` repositories are counted, never listed (GH-014, OPEN-33 default).

source.description: Which plane produced this artifact. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders such an artifact is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it (FS-10 §2 v0 note; the edge route answers `sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). `registry-v0` is the P-M2 production source of record — the curated registry repository the index is built from. `platform` is the P-M3 producer of record — the platform database, rendered by `jobs.index-build`. Optional, and its absence asserts nothing: an artifact whose body cannot carry the label borrows the plane's declaration from `/registry/index/meta.json`. The enum widens additively when the P-M3 producer takes a value of its own, and `platform` (2026-09-12) is that widening: `jobs.index-build` writes it in `PSN_ENV=prod` and writes `fixture` in every other environment, so a reader can still tell a production plane from a synthetic one by the label alone.

shard.description: Shard key: a single lowercased first character of the repository name, `0` for non-alphabetic names, or the literal `export` for the bulk document.

count.description: Number of entries in THIS document. Registry-wide totals live in the index meta document.

ownerOrgId.description: The owner node_id the curated record carries as `owner_node_id` (`O_…` or `U_…`) — the same value `repo-record.v1` publishes as `owner.orgId`, and the key a Portfolio Entitlement's `scope.org` names (ops decision D42). On the entry so a Portfolio picker or a scanner can list an owner's repositories from the index alone. Absent when the registry records none. `owner` stays a display-cache login.

adoptedAt.description: Adoption date. `recentlyRegistered` ordering on the browse landing view uses this — cold-start fairness (WEB-073).

language.description: Primary language, for the browse facet (WEB-071 v0 subset). Null when GitHub reports none.

summary.description: Optional display summary echoed from PURPOSE.yml. Repository content — escaped on render.

recordUrl.description: URL of this repository's repo record artifact.

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id, in either of the two forms GitHub has issued: the opaque current form (a repository's is `R_`-prefixed) and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository` and whose `=` padding the first alternative cannot express. Widened 2026-09-08 to admit the second: `registry-v0-record.v1` accepts both, so a record the curated registry accepts is publishable in this artifact. The primary key for repositories and people throughout this contract set (FS-00 §6.1).

githubOwnerNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL node_id of a repository OWNER in the current global-id form (`O_…` organisation, `U_…` user), as `registry-v0-record.v1` `$defs.githubOwnerNodeId` defines it. Local to this file because schemas here carry no cross-file `$ref`. Narrower than `githubNodeId` on purpose: that pattern would also admit a login such as `helvetica-tools`.
